messages:
Maya Patel: Hi all, first week onboarding question. I'm trying to run the sample job in the playground namespace but `kubectl get ns playground` returns nothing. I'm on macOS and used the Okta SSO flow to get my kubeconfig.

Rory Kim: welcome Maya! :wave: quick checks: `kubectl config current-context`, `kubectl config view --minify`, and `kubectl get namespaces`. Also make sure the cluster you logged into is `gke-redwood-dev`.

Maya Patel: current-context -> `redwood-dev`. `kubectl config view --minify` shows user `maya@okta`. `kubectl get namespaces` lists default, kube-system, etc but no playground.

Rory Kim: interesting. Two possibilities: you're pointed at the wrong cluster (similar name) or playground is in a different project/cluster. Run `kubectl config get-contexts --no-headers` and paste output.

Maya Patel:```
CURRENT   NAME            CLUSTER             AUTHINFO
*         redwood-dev     gke-redwood-dev     maya@okta
          redwood-staging gke-redwood-stg      maya@okta
```

Rory Kim: Ok that's the dev cluster. Playground should exist there. Try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playground` — if no, it's an RBAC problem.

Maya Patel: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playground` -> "no".

Rory Kim: That confirms it. For new hires we either grant a namespaced RoleBinding or give you a short-lived service account token to use. Which do you prefer?

Maya Patel: whichever is fastest to get me unblocked now. For future automation I want SA flow, but today RoleBinding is fine.

Rory Kim: cool. I'll create a temporary RoleBinding that grants `edit` on `playground` to your Okta identity. @eng-infra-bot can you make a ticket?

eng-infra-bot: Created INFRA-3312: "playground access for new hire Maya Patel" assigned to @platform-oncall (ETA 1.5h).

platform-oncall: Hi Maya, I've applied a namespaced RoleBinding in `playground` for `maya@okta` with TTL 24h. Please run:

```
kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playground
kubectl get pods -n playground
```

Maya Patel: running... `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n playground` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n playground` -> "NAME READY STATUS..." lists 7 pods. Great, I can proceed. Thanks! :tada: 

Rory Kim: great. When you have a minute, consider switching to the SA token flow for tooling. Steps we suggest (k8s v1.24+):

```
# create ephemeral token for team SA
kubectl create token onboarding-sa -n playground
# create local kubeconfig user and context
kubectl config set-credentials onboarding-sa-user --token="$(kubectl create token onboarding-sa -n playground)"
kubectl config set-context onboarding-sa-context --cluster=gke-redwood-dev --user=onboarding-sa-user --namespace=playground
kubectl config use-context onboarding-sa-context
```

Rory Kim: Note: our platform rotates projected tokens and for anything long-lived we use the secrets service + short TTL. Ask infra if you need a longer-lived integration token.

Maya Patel: saved. One quick follow-up: where is the onboarding checklist updated so I can mark this done?

platform-oncall: I've updated ONBOARD-91 with access granted and linked INFRA-3312. You're good to check off the K8s access step.

Maya Patel: Awesome, thanks everyone!"
